Chapter 8: Lessons Learned – The Fragility of International Justice
When you look back at the journey for justice in Kosovo, it’s impossible not to reflect on both the victories and the disappointments. For everyone involved, those years brought powerful lessons. Maybe the biggest one? International justice is far more fragile than we’d like to believe. Good intentions alone rarely get the job done.
Picture a prosecutor, years after the whirlwind of the tribunal. She remembers that sense of urgency that fueled her every day—the belief that the law could bring order to chaos, that the world was ready to stand behind real accountability. But, as the years ticked by, she saw just how easily justice could slip through our fingers—snagged by politics, slowed down by indifference, and tangled up in the sheer complexity of the mission.
The tribunal’s limits became painfully clear. It relied on countries working together, but every nation had its own interests to protect. Evidence got lost or hidden, witnesses were scared into silence, and political pressure crept in from all sides. The process dragged on—sometimes feeling impossibly slow. And for every small win, there was a setback: cases collapsed, suspects vanished, and sometimes, the truth was just out of reach.
Still, there were moments that truly mattered. The tribunal set brand-new precedents. It proved that even the most powerful could face justice. It built a record—a real, undeniable account of what happened, something no one could easily erase. And for those who suffered, it offered at least a measure of justice, even if it wasn’t perfect.
The lessons from Kosovo echoed far beyond the Balkans. They changed how the world responded to crises in places like Darfur and Syria. The experience made it clear: international justice is possible, but it’s incredibly fragile. It depends on political will, on ordinary people caring enough to pay attention, and on the courage of those who dare to speak out.
For the people who were part of this journey, the process was humbling. They learned that justice isn’t a destination you reach and then rest—it’s a winding road, full of setbacks and disappointment, but also hope. The search for truth is never simple, but it’s always worth the effort.
Kosovo’s story became a kind of cautionary tale. It reminds us that the promise of justice has to be renewed every time a new challenge appears. We can’t just look away, even when the task feels impossible. And perhaps, above all, it offered hope—a hope rooted in the resilience of those who refuse to give up, no matter how tough the road gets.
